 In The High Court At Calcutta
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction

Appellate Side  Present:
 The Hon'ble Justice Biswaroop Chowdhury  F.M.A. 456 of 2009  Smt. Dhirenbala Mondal  VERSUS  United India Insurance Company Limited & Anr.
For the appellant: Mr. Krishanu Banik, Adv.
 Mr. Tathagata Banik, Adv.
For the respondents: Mr. Arabinda Kundu, Adv.
Last Heard on: November 12, 2025 Judgment on: December 02, 2025 Biswaroop Chowdhury,J:
The Appellant before this Court was a claimant in a Motor Accident claim case under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act1988 and is aggrieved by the Judgment and Award dated 16/07/2008 passed by Learned Additional District Judge 4th Court Paschim Medinipur in MACC Case No. 68/07.
The case of the claimant/Appellant before the Learned Trial Court may be summed up thus:
On 01.01.2007 at about 9A.M. the deceased along with Kajal Patra was by the extreme left side of the road running by the side of the Masanta Pukar subsidiary Health Centre when the offending Tractor dashed them with a high speed when they became severely injured and died.

The deceased used to earn Rs. 8,000/- to Rs.
10,000/- per month from this cultivation and business and the claimant was completely dependent on her husbands income.
The Respondent no-1 contested the case by filing written statement denying the allegations made therein.
Pursuant to filing of written statement issues were framed, and upon hearing the parties and Smt. Dhirenbala Mondal vs United India Insurance Company Limited ...

1 considering the evidence adduced Learned Trial Court was pleased to dispose the claim case by observing and directing as follows:
'Hence Ordered that the MAC case be and the same is allowed in Part on contest against the Ins. Co./O.P. without any cost and same is allowed in part on contest against the non-contesting O.P./owner of the vehicle but without any cost.

The applicant is entitled to final compensation of Rs. 55,000/- from the opposite parties,
and Opposite Parties are jointly liable to pay that compensation to the applicant.

But at this stage the Insurance Company is hereby directed to pay the amount of Rs.
55,000/- by passing an MIS in the name of applicant Smt. Dhiren Bala Mondal, w/o,
Late Gunadhar Mondal in any post office as per her choice within two months from the date of receipt of this order taking help of the applicant and as and when MIS should be opened the said amount of cheque shall be deposited in the name of said post Master for opening MIS in the name of Smt. Dhiren Bala Mondal and applicant shall have to meet the officer of the Present Insurance Company and give such consent regarding selections of the post office for opening MIS in respect of that amount and if applicant does not help in this regard in that case there is no liability on behalf of the Insurance Company to pay any interest for not opening the MIS because it is the duty of the applicant to take such step for opening MIS and shall have to take such help from the Insurance Company and Insurance Company shall have to act accordingly.
But before depositing the cheque against the MIS, the Insurance Company shall be satisfied that applicant has deposited the Deficit Court Fees of Rs. 2,990/-.'
The Appellant/Claimant being aggrieved by the Judgment and Order dated 18th July 2008 passed by Learned Additional District Judge 4th Court Paschim Medinipur has come up with this instant appeal.

It is the contention of the Appellant that the Learned Trial Court erred in law and in fact in awarding the inadequate compensation of Rs. 55,000/- towards the claimant for motor accidental death of the victim in the motor accident which occurred on 01.01.2007.
It is further contended that the Learned Trial Judge was wrong in disbelieving the fact that the victim deceased did not die due to rash and negligent driving of the driving of the offending vehicle.
It is also contended that the Learned Trial Judge erred in not computing the compensation as per income of the deceased.
Heard Learned Advocate for the Appellant and Learned Advocate for the Respondent no-1.
Perused the materials on record.
Learned Advocate for the Appellant submits that the Learned Trial Court came to an erroneous finding with regard to the death of the victim which was by road accident.

Learned Advocate further draws attention to the evidence of P.W. 4 Ajit Mondal and submits that the evidence of the said witness will go to show that death of the victim took place due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle being WB-33A/1664 but the Learned Trial Judge came to a finding that death of the victim took place due to fall from vehicle which is not the case of either party.

Learned Advocate also submits the Smt. Dhirenbala Mondal vs United India Insurance Company Limited ... on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192387979/

sentences.text: compensation is awarded not on the basis of the income of the victim or notional income but simply a one time compensation.
Learned Advocate for the respondent no-1 submits that the claimant/appellant failed to prove the income of the victim and well as the accident.
Learned Advocate further submits that the evidence of the claimants will go to show that death of the victim took place due to fall from vehicle and there is no rash driving of the vehicle.
Learned Advocate also submits that there is no error in the Judgment of the Learned Trial Court.
Before proceeding to decide on the material in issue it is necessary to consider the evidence of P.W. 4, who claimed to be the eye witness of the accident.
P.W.-4 in his examination in chief has stated that he is the eye witness of the occurrence.

On 01-01-2007 when he was going towards their paddy and at that time his father and one Kajal Patra were sitting by the extreme left side of the road and taking sun-ray.
At that time one tractor bearing no. WB-33A/1664 was coming in a rash and negligent manner endangering human life and safety to its extreme right side and dashed his father and said Kajal Patra. Both of them died on the spot.
In cross examination P.W. 4 stated that the tractor did not overturn on the spot.
He further stated that the side of front wheel touched the arm-pit of his father.
He also stated that he saw the tractor to come but found that his father and the other person did not sit encroaching the said road.
He denied the suggestion that he was not present at the spot.

Upon perusing the findings of the Learned Trial Judge it appears that the Learned Trial Judge based his findings on the cross examination of P.W. 4 that his father did not sit encroaching the road and it is not the case that his father was not at all sitting on the road.
Further the statement in the cross examination that the tractor was empty and the tractor did not overturn was not taken into consideration.
In the examination in chief P.W. 4 stated that the tractor dashed his father and Kajal Patra.
In cross examination P.W. 4 stated that the side of front wheel touched the arm pit of his father.
Thus it is clear from cross examination that the injury is caused by the front wheel of the tractor.
There is no reason to hold that the victim was within the tractor, as when a person is within the tractor there is no chance of getting injured by the wheel.

Further the Learned Judge went on to hold that the victim fell down from the tractor when it is not the case of the claimant or the opposite party that the victim fell down from the vehicle, and there is no suggestion put to the witness there is no scope for the Court to proceed with that assumption, and make observations.

The claimants/appellants apart from adducing oral evidence have filed copy of FIR,
INQUEST Report which states that the victim Gunadhar Mondal was dashed by tractor.

sentences.text: Thus the documents filed corroborate the case of the Appellant/Claimants.
Thus the appellant has been able to prove that death of the victim Gunadhar Mondal was due to rash and negligent driving of tractor no-WB-33A/664.
The findings of the Learned Trial Court is thus set aside.
The claimant is entitled to compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act.

Now with regard to the Quantum of Compensation it appears that although evidence was adduced that the victim used to earn Rs. 8,000/- to Rs. 10,000/- per month but the said income could not be proved.
Thus notional income of Rs. 3000/- is taken into consideration.
Thus the Annul income comes to Rs. 36,000/- 1/3rd is deducted on account of Personal Expenses, and the annual income comes to Rs. 24,000/-.
10% should be added an account of future prospect.

Thus annual dependency loss comes to Rs.
26,400/-.
As the victim was 58 years old multiplier of 9 should be applied thus total dependency loss comes to Rs. 2,37,600/-.
General Loss of Rs. 70,000/- on account of loss of Estate Funeral expenses and consortium should be added.
Thus Total loss comes to Rs. 3,07,600/-.

Thus the Appellant claimant is entitled to Rs. 3,07,600/-
compensation from Respondent no-1.

The Respondent no-1 is thus directed to deposit before Registrar General, High Court, Calcutta Rs. 3,07,600/- (Rupees three lakhs seven thousand six hundred)
within 5 weeks along with interest from the date of filing of claim case till date of this order..

In the event Rs. 55,000/- as directed by Learned Trial Court is already paid,
the balance amount with interest be deposited.

Upon such deposit, being made,
claimant/Appellant may withdraw the same upon compliance of requisite formalities.
Urgent photostat certified copy of this order, if applied for, should be made available to the parties upon compliance with the requisite formalities.

(Biswaroop Chowdhury, J.)
